perche: Z-C21.13, finding C5-7. Until library 0.143.0 the STEP export wrote AP242 by setting the preference swStepAP to 242, a value its page does not list (swconst help page FileSaveAsSTEPOptions.htm: «203 = STEP AP203 format», «214 = STEP AP214 format»). The probe probe_step_ap242 of 29/9/2026 measured it: 242 is accepted and read back as 242, SaveAs3 answers true with no error and no warning, and the file is AP203 (FILE_SCHEMA «CONFIG_CONTROL_DESIGN»). The FILE_SCHEMA check refused that file, but for the wrong reason (AP242 asked, AP203 out), after replacing whatever file was at the path. AP242 has another door, IModelDocExtension.PublishSTEP242File (SOLIDWORKS MBD), which the same probe measured answering 4, swPublishStep242_MBDLicenseNotAvailable, with a .stp path on this machine. The fix never writes 242 into swStepAP, brings our part to the front, calls PublishSTEP242File, and on 4 refuses saying that AP242 needs the SOLIDWORKS MBD licence and that AP214 and AP203 remain.
il_difetto_che_questo_caso_prende: The refusal with the wrong reason. On 0.143.0 this step also fails, but its message says that AP242 was asked and AP203 came out, and names neither SOLIDWORKS MBD nor swPublishStep242_MBDLicenseNotAvailable: the case is red there on the message, and green once the refusal says why.
on_a_machine_with_mbd: MACHINE-DEPENDENT. The answer comes from the licence of the machine that runs the bench, not from the part: the bench machine has no SOLIDWORKS MBD licence (probe of 29/9/2026, code 4). On a machine WITH that licence PublishSTEP242File answers 0, the file goes through the same FILE_SCHEMA check as AP203 and AP214, and this step no longer fails: there the case turns red for a good reason, and must become a success case that expects AP242 as the protocol that came out (that branch is not measured anywhere yet).
shared_argument_with_the_twin: The reopen-and-compare flag is the argument in common with the twin, which the bench asks for (a twin must share at least one argument with the same value). The refusal comes before any reopening.
